summary: Establishes the lean multidisciplinary team and product practices needed to deliver King’s Edge, support the focused first Digital Student Experience Hub release and learn what enduring digital product capability King’s requires.
detailSummary:
Digital Innovation and Product Development Capability establishes the team and working practices through which King’s Edge and the first Digital Student Experience Hub release are delivered. During 2026/27, the capability itself is part of the discovery: King’s tests how much core capacity is needed, which specialist inputs must be reliably available, and which product and operating practices are required for sustainable delivery.

The funded Year One baseline is a lean four-person core: two full-stack engineers, one product and experience designer and one agile delivery manager, with hands-on technical leadership within the engineering capacity. The substantive build demand remains King’s Edge. The same team establishes the reusable Hub foundations and focused first-release experience under 4.1.2.

Broad Year One Hub discovery is intentionally larger than the four-person build pod. It therefore requires protected service-design and business-analysis capacity and reliable user-research support alongside the core team, with the first assumption being existing or seconded institutional capability rather than automatic permanent recruitment. Architecture, data, integration, security, accessibility, testing and live-service specialists are drawn in on a time-bound basis as the work requires them.

By the end of Year One, King’s should have both delivered product capability and evidence about the capability model itself. Actual throughput, quality, discovery demand, integration effort, specialist dependencies and live-service obligations should determine the team shape and investment required in Years Two and Three.

caseForChange.problem:
King’s does not currently have a sufficiently dependable multidisciplinary product capability for turning emerging student-experience needs into working, supported digital services at pace. Requirements can be addressed through conventional system change, local initiatives, temporary projects or standalone products, making prioritisation and reuse difficult.

King’s now needs enough in-house capability to deliver a substantial King’s Edge roadmap and establish the first Digital Student Experience Hub foundations, while also supporting broader discovery of the student digital estate. The permanent team shape is not yet known well enough to justify designing it in advance.
caseForChange.opportunity:
A lean funded product core, combined with protected discovery capacity and time-bound specialist support, gives King’s a disciplined route from need to supported change without overbuilding the permanent organisation before evidence exists. One transparent pipeline can connect prioritisation, research, service design, product design, engineering, assurance, release and learning.

King’s Edge supplies the first substantive product demand. The Digital Student Experience Hub extends that work into reusable shared foundations and a focused institutional release, while broad discovery informs the next phase.
caseForChange.whyNow:
King’s Edge creates an immediate requirement for dependable in-house digital product delivery. At the same time, the Digital Student Experience Hub needs a focused September 2027 first release and a wider evidence base for the remainder of the mobilisation.

2026/27 is therefore the right point to mobilise the four-person core, protect additional discovery capacity, and learn through real delivery. Future expansion should follow evidence about throughput, journey demand, integration complexity, quality and operational load.
caseForChange.intendedChange:
King’s has a dependable multidisciplinary digital product capability with a transparent pipeline, clear decision rights and repeatable practices for discovery, design, engineering, quality, assurance, release and continuous improvement.

During 2026/27, the funded four-person core delivers the King’s Edge replatform and agreed product roadmap and supports the focused first Digital Student Experience Hub release. Protected service-design, business-analysis and user-research capacity enables the broader Hub discovery without silently consuming the build pod.

The capability can then expand or change shape where live demand and evidence justify it, with future staffing and recurrent costs confirmed through the wider three-year mobilisation business case rather than carried forward as automatic assumptions.

benefits.title: King’s responds more quickly to emerging student needs
benefits.statement: Priority needs can be translated into tested digital responses in shorter cycles, with student and staff evidence shaping development before large commitments are made.
benefits.realisationPeriod: From establishment of the first delivery pipeline
benefits.successLooksLike: Priority needs move predictably from discovery to evaluated live use, and users can influence solutions while they remain adaptable.

benefits.title: Digital delivery becomes more predictable and evidence-led
benefits.statement: A transparent pipeline, explicit capacity decisions and consistent product and assurance practices make needs, priorities, progress and trade-offs clearer.
benefits.beneficiary: Students, service owners, Digital and IT and King’s
benefits.realisationPeriod: As the operating model becomes routine
benefits.successLooksLike: Demand is prioritised through one route, delivery commitments are visible and changes in team capacity can be explained by actual roadmap evidence.

benefits.title: Successful innovation becomes sustainable institutional provision
benefits.statement: Valuable changes have a defined route into secure, supported and appropriately owned operation, while multidisciplinary capability remains available for continuous improvement.
benefits.beneficiary: Students, service owners, Digital and IT and King’s
benefits.successLooksLike: Successful capabilities have explicit ownership and support arrangements, unsuccessful trials close cleanly, and the product capability has an evidence-based route into business as usual.

steps.title: Recruit and mobilise the core multidisciplinary digital product team
steps.summary: Recruit, appoint or assign the four-person first-year core from September through November 2026: two full-stack engineers, one product and experience designer and one agile delivery manager. Confirm protected service-design and business-analysis capacity, reliable user-research support and named time-bound technical specialists from appropriate institutional teams.

steps.title: Establish the product operating model and delivery practices
steps.summary: From November 2026 to February 2027, establish one transparent pipeline, prioritisation and capacity cadence, proportionate discovery and user involvement, engineering and quality expectations, embedded assurance and release practices across King’s Edge and the Digital Student Experience Hub.

steps.title: Prove the capability through King’s Edge, broad discovery and the focused Hub release
steps.summary: From January to October 2027, prove that the core team can deliver the substantive King’s Edge roadmap and focused Digital Student Experience Hub release while protected discovery capacity maps the wider estate and priority journeys. Use evidence to identify real capacity gaps before expanding the team.

steps.title: Make product operations and live-service collaboration routine
steps.summary: From November 2027 to February 2028, make operating practices routine across the live Digital Student Experience Hub and King’s Edge product domain, balancing roadmap delivery, incidents, maintenance, quality, discovery and continuous improvement.

steps.title: Scale the team and its practices where the wider roadmap justifies it
steps.summary: From March to October 2028, expand or reshape the core and specialist capability only where live-service evidence, broad discovery and the confirmed wider student-journey roadmap justify additional throughput or expertise.

steps.title: Embed an enduring institutional product-development capability
steps.summary: By the end of the three-year mobilisation, establish the sustainable multidisciplinary capability, professional leadership, governance, product practices and interfaces with SED product ownership and Digital and IT specialist/platform services. Confirm recurrent staffing and costs from live evidence before business-as-usual transition.
